Subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data isolation follow-up

Hi Lina —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on FinSecure's data isolation requirements:

Summary of what I heard:
- Primary requirement: no customer data (payload, prompts, or inference outputs) can be accessible by other tenants or leave your VPC without explicit approval.
- Must support customer-managed KMS for any stored artifacts and keys (HSM/KMS integration).
- Auditability: per-request audit logs, retention controls, and exportable logs for your security team.
- Data residency: us-east-1 preference, with strict egress controls.

How Redwood deployment options map to those needs (high level):
- Hosted API: not recommended for FinSecure given the strict isolation + KMS requirements — shared multitenant control plane and no customer-managed KMS option today.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): provides a dedicated GPU pool and logical separation at the serving layer. Good for predictable throughput and cost, but control plane and some support tooling (logs/metrics) remain with Redwood-managed infrastructure. We can limit data flows, but Dedicated does not offer a full customer-managed networking plane by default.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): provides the strongest isolation — private control plane, optional VPC peering or direct connect, customer-managed networking, and options for on-prem/air-gapped deployments. This is the configuration that best meets your “no egress of payload” and HSM/KMS requirements.

Requested items / next steps:
1) I will send our SOC 2 Type II brief and a short Private deployment architecture doc (attached).
2) Can you confirm whether FinSecure requires fully air-gapped on-prem deployment or VPC peering to a cloud VPC (us-east-1) would be sufficient?
3) Please share the name and contact for your infra/security lead to join a technical deep-dive next week (we recommended 45–60 minutes).
4) If you agree, we'll schedule a tech call to map exact controls (KMS integration points, logging endpoints, and network egress rules) and then follow with a draft Mutual Action Plan.

Rough timelines to expect: Dedicated can often be provisioned in ~2–4 weeks depending on capacity and scope; Private VPC/on-prem typically requires ~6–8 weeks for initial setup and validation (customer-dependent). We'll provide a more specific estimate once we align on the connectivity model.

Thanks — I'll attach the docs and follow up with availability options for the technical call.

Best,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A couple of clarifying questions before we book the tech call: 

1) For Dedicated, can you confirm whether payloads (prompts + responses) are ever written to any shared storage or logs that Redwood or other tenants could access? FinSecure policy requires no shared storage of plaintext customer data.
2) If we went Dedicated, is there an option to disable telemetry/logging at the service level so that only perf/health metrics (no payloads) are retained?
3) For Private VPC, what is the default behavior for support access? Is there an option for emergency access with customer approval only, or does Redwood retain a break-glass mechanism?
4) Ballpark pricing — you mentioned Dedicated could be cheaper than Private. Can you give a rough delta or point me to a pricing example so we can start budget conversations?

Apologies for the number of questions — we just want to avoid surprises during procurement. My infra lead is Simon Park (simon.park@finsecure.com); please include him on the tech call.

Hi Lina —

Great questions — answers below and I've included Mateo (our solutions architect) to join the technical deep-dive.

Q1 — Dedicated and storage of payloads:
- Dedicated provides dedicated GPU capacity and logical tenant separation, but the control plane (and the management plane for logs/metrics) is still Redwood-managed. We do NOT store plaintext customer payloads in shared long-term storage by default. However, for debugging/troubleshooting we may retain traces/logs in our internal logging infrastructure unless you opt-out. We can agree to a contract clause restricting retention of plaintext payloads and ensure any temporary traces are scrubbed or available only under specific incident procedures.

Q2 — Telemetry/logging options on Dedicated:
- Yes — we can disable payload-level telemetry and restrict logs to aggregated performance/health metrics. That configuration would need to be captured in the MSA/SLA and implemented as part of provisioning.

Q3 — Support access / break-glass for Private VPC:
- Private VPC is designed for customer-managed control plane and minimizes Redwood access. By default, there is no persistent Redwood access to your private control plane. Emergency support access is configurable: options include (a) no external support access (you're fully responsible), (b) role-based emergency access requiring an approved short-lived token from FinSecure, or (c) a break-glass workflow that requires documented approval. We can build the model you prefer and put it into the security addendum.

Q4 — Ballpark pricing:
- Ballpark: Dedicated reserved pool starts materially lower than Private since Private includes networking, custom onboarding, and often a control-plane license. Typical delta ranges 20–40% depending on scale and connectivity. Mateo can provide a more detailed pricing example during the tech call.

- If we align on Private, we'll draft a Mutual Action Plan that covers connectivity, KMS integration, and the security addendum.
